To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the canine MTD is a better predictor of human toxicity for bizelesin than is the murine MDT.
the canine CFU-gms are more sensitive to the myelotoxic effects of bizelesion than the murine and human CFU-gms, which may be a more appropriate model to use to determine the MTD for clinical trials.

the in vitro clonal assay results were consistent with those seen clinically in vivo and that the canine MTD is better than the mouse MTD for predicting the safe starting dose of bizelesin for clinical trials.

the in vitro effects of the bifunctioal alkylating agents, bizelesin and CC-1065, on the human, canine and mouse myeloid progenitors.
the pharmacodynamics of bizelesin, a novel anticancer drug, on human, canine, and murine hematopoietic progenitor cells.
the development of new anticancer agents and the preclinical evaluation of these agents for their efficacy and safety in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the canine model is more predictive of the clinical response to bizelesin than the murine model.
the dog is more sensitive than the mouse to bizelesin myelotoxicity and is the better model to predict human toxicity.
the canine MTD is a more reliable predictor of the human MTD than the murine model for the myelosuppressant effects of bizelesins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the in vitro sensitivity and the time dependence of myelotoxicity of CFU-gm are qualitatively similar to the results seen in vivo in dogs and mice.

the in vitro pharmacodynamic data for human CFUgms is qualitatively consistent and quantitative consistent with the preclinical animal studies, suggesting the canine model is a better predictor of human toxicity.
the canine MTD of bizelesin is the most predictive for the MTD of human clinical trials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
preclinical animal species should be chosen based on their pharmacodynamics and not only on their pharmacokinetics.
the canine model is the best preclinical model for the evaluation of the myelotoxic effects of bizelesion.

preclinical studies should include a species that closely models the human response in vivo and that pharmacodynamic studies in clonal assays can help identify the most appropriate species to use in these studies.
